metadata.title: Special Stable Matrices and Their Non-square Counterpart

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Sufficient DUS Condition for Non-square Systems)
nodes.statement: For a proper and asymptotically stable non-square system H(s) in C^{m x n} with steady state transfer matrix A = H(0) in R^{n x m}, if there exists a block diagonal non-square matrix K such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices E and all j in the index set M, Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0, then the non-square system can be controlled by a distributed integral controller and achieve Decentralized Unconditional Stability.
assumptions: H(s) is a proper and asymptotically stable non-square system in C^{m x n}
A = H(0) in R^{n x m} is the steady state transfer matrix

There exists a block diagonal non-square matrix K in C^{n x m} such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices E in R^{n x n} and j in M (index set of k-tuples of integers in range 1,...,m), Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0
conclusions: The non-square system can be controlled by a distributed integral controller and achieve Decentralized Unconditional Stability

nodes.name: Definition 1 (Squared Matrices)
nodes.statement: For a non-square matrix A in R^{m x n} and its associated block diagonal matrix K, squared matrices are constructed by selecting one column from each group of columns of A. The m-order squared matrices [A]^m_{s_i} are formed by choosing one column per group (yielding N = prod(p_i) matrices), and lower-order squared matrices [A]^k_{s_i} with k < m arise when all control inputs for certain groups have zero gain.

nodes.name: Definition 2 (D-stable and Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrices)
nodes.statement: A matrix A in R^{n x n} is D-stable if DA is stable for all diagonal matrices D > 0. A matrix A is Volterra-Lyapunov stable if there exists a diagonal matrix D > 0 for which AD + DA^T > 0.

nodes.name: Definition 3 (Strictly Column Diagonally Dominant)
nodes.statement: A square matrix A is strictly column diagonally dominant if for each row i, the absolute value of the diagonal element is greater than the sum of the absolute values of the other elements in the same column: |a_{ii}| >= sum_{j>i} |a_{ij}| for all i.

nodes.name: Definition 4 (Strictly Column Diagonally Balanced Dominant)
nodes.statement: A matrix A is strictly column diagonally balanced dominant if there exists a diagonal matrix D such that |AD| + |DA^T| is strictly column diagonally dominant. If additionally all diagonal elements of AD + DA^T are positive, then A is called positive diagonally balanced dominant.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (Volterra-Lyapunov implies D-stability of submatrices)
nodes.statement: If a matrix A in R^{n x n} is Volterra-Lyapunov stable, then for any diagonal positive matrix D > 0 and any index set j in M, Re{sigma([AD]_j)} > 0, which implies that all principal submatrices [A]_j are D-stable.
assumptions: A = (a_{ij}) in R^{n x n} is Volterra-Lyapunov stable
conclusions: For any diagonal positive matrix D > 0 and j in M (index set of k-tuples in range 1,...,m), Re{sigma([AD]_j)} > 0
All submatrices [A]_j for j in M are D-stable matrices

nodes.name: Definition 5 (Individual Volterra-Lyapunov Stable Non-square Matrix)
nodes.statement: A real non-square matrix A in R^{m x n} is individual Volterra-Lyapunov stable if one can find an individual diagonal positive matrix D_i > 0 for each m-order squared matrix [A]^m_{s_i} such that [A]^m_{s_i} D_i + D_i ([A]^m_{s_i})^T > 0.

nodes.name: Definition 6 (Simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov Stable Non-square Matrix)
nodes.statement: A real non-square matrix A in R^{m x n} is simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stable if one can find a single diagonal positive matrix D > 0 such that for all m-order squared matrices [A]^m_{s_i}, the LMI [A]^m_{s_i} D + D ([A]^m_{s_i})^T > 0 holds.

nodes.name: Definition 7 (Simultaneous Positive Diagonally Balanced Dominant Non-square Matrix)
nodes.statement: A real non-square matrix A in R^{m x n} is simultaneous positive diagonally balanced dominant if one can find a diagonal positive matrix D > 0 such that [A]^m_{s_i} D + D ([A]^m_{s_i})^T are all strictly column diagonally dominant with positive diagonal elements for all m-order squared matrices.

nodes.name: Note 1 (Simultaneous positive diagonally balanced dominant implies simultaneous VL stable)
nodes.statement: A non-square matrix A is simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stable if it is simultaneous positive diagonally balanced dominant.

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (Card Combination Payoff Lemma)
nodes.statement: Consider m groups of cards where group i has p_i distinct cards. A player bets on combinations of m cards (one per group) with positive payoffs gamma. If the payoffs satisfy gamma_{(1,...,1)} = 1 and the ratio condition gamma_{(...,j,...)} = gamma_{(...,1,...)} * kappa_{ij}, then the player can implement a desired strategy with specified ratios kappa_{kj} > 0 between cards within each group.
assumptions: There are m groups of cards, group i containing p_i distinct cards
The payoffs satisfy: gamma_{(zeta_1,...,j,...,zeta_m)} = gamma_{(zeta_1,...,1,...,zeta_m)} * kappa_{ij} (ratio preservation)
conclusions: The player can implement the desired strategy achieving the specified ratios kappa_{kj} > 0 between cards within each group

nodes.name: Lemma 3 (Simultaneous VL stable implies non-square D-stable-like)
nodes.statement: If a real non-square matrix A in R^{m x n} is simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stable, then there exists a block diagonal non-square matrix K in C^{n x m} such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices E and j in M, Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0.
assumptions: A in R^{m x n} is a simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrix (Definition 6)
conclusions: There exists a block diagonal non-square matrix K in C^{n x m} such that for all non-negative diagonal E in R^{n x n} and j in M, Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0

nodes.name: Note 2 (Interpretation of Lemma 3)
nodes.statement: Lemma 3 confirms that a non-square simultaneously Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrix is also a non-square D-stable-like matrix. The simultaneous condition implies a common diagonal Lyapunov function for all m-order squared matrices, which can even guarantee instantaneous switching stability.

nodes.name: Note 3 (Strength of simultaneous condition)
nodes.statement: The simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stability condition in Lemma 3 is strong especially when N is large. Theorem 2 relaxes this to individual Volterra-Lyapunov stability for a special class of matrices.

nodes.name: Lemma 4 (Equivalence for normal matrices in class F)
nodes.statement: For normal matrices in the class F = {A : a_{ij} >= 0 for all i != j}, D-stability and Volterra-Lyapunov stability are both equivalent to stability.
assumptions: A is in the class F = {A : a_{ij} >= 0 for all i != j}
conclusions: D-stability and Volterra-Lyapunov stability are equivalent to stability

nodes.name: Lemma 5 (Equivalence of stability notions for normal matrices in class F)
nodes.statement: For a set of normal matrices in class F, D-stability, individual Volterra-Lyapunov stability, and simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stability are all equivalent to stability.
assumptions: A set of normal matrices which are in class F = {A : a_{ij} >= 0 for all i != j}
conclusions: D-stability, individual Volterra-Lyapunov stability, and simultaneous Volterra-Lyapunov stability are all equivalent to stability

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Non-square D-stable-like condition for normal matrices in class F)
nodes.statement: If all m-th order squared matrices of A in R^{m x n} are normal matrices in class F and are D-stable, then there exists a block diagonal non-square matrix K such that for all non-negative diagonal matrices E and j in M, Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0.
assumptions: A in R^{m x n} is a real non-square matrix
All m-th order squared matrices [A]^m_{s_i} are normal matrices
All m-th order squared matrices [A]^m_{s_i} are in class F = {A : a_{ij} >= 0 for all i != j}
All m-th order squared matrices [A]^m_{s_i} are D-stable
conclusions: There exists a block diagonal non-square matrix K in C^{n x m} such that for all non-negative diagonal E in R^{n x n} and j in M, Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0

nodes.name: Conjecture 1 (Individual VL stability suffices for non-square D-stable-like condition)
nodes.statement: If a real non-square matrix A in R^{m x n} is an individual Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrix (each squared matrix has its own diagonal D_i making [A]^m_{s_i} D_i + D_i ([A]^m_{s_i})^T > 0), then there exists a block diagonal K such that Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0 for all non-negative diagonal E and j in M.
assumptions: A in R^{m x n} is an individual Volterra-Lyapunov stable matrix (Definition 5)
conclusions: There exists a block diagonal non-square matrix K in C^{n x m} such that for all non-negative diagonal E in R^{n x n} and j in M, Re{sigma_i([AEK]_j)} > 0

nodes.name: Note 4 (Partial results on conjecture)
nodes.statement: The conjecture can be proved with extra conditions, for example if redundant inputs are only in one channel the proof becomes straightforward, but the general case remains open.

nodes.name: Block Diagonal K Matrix Structure (Eq. 2)
nodes.statement: The block diagonal matrix K in R^{n x m} (transposed) has non-negative entries k_{i,j} arranged so that each block row i has p_i entries, with sum p_i = n. This defines the grouping structure for columns of A.

nodes.name: AEK Column Expression (Eq. 4)
nodes.statement: The product AEK can be expressed as columns that are weighted linear combinations of grouped columns of A: AEK = [sum epsilon_{1,i} k_{1,i} a_{1,i}, ..., sum epsilon_{m,i} k_{m,i} a_{m,i}], showing how the non-square product reduces to m columns via the K structure.
